total decentralization performs best in situations in which there is a great deal of information available to the decision makers, the decision makers are not required to be too accurate, and the coordination penalty is not too high.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of a decentralized decision-making mechanism can be superior to a centralized decision-making mechanism.
, in the class of linear decision-making situations, total decentralization and centralization are not necessarily equivalent in performance.

the performance of total decentralizaton is better than that of total centralization for most of the situations studied, but there are situations in which total decentralization performs very badly, and total centralization is the better alternative.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimal structure of the decision-making mechanism is not always centralized or decentralized, but depends on the structure of the information and the penalties involved.
the performance of total decentralizations and total centralizations depends on the specific decision-making problem and cannot be determined a priori.

, in a linear decision-making situation, there are no general rules for determining whether total centralization or total decentralization will perform better than the other; the performance of the two mechanisms depends critically on the specific decision-making situation.
